arml-2023-superrelay-01.title: Smallest number
arml-2023-superrelay-01.body:
A number just above $2023$ of the form $20XY$ has digit sum $2+X+Y=17$, so $X+Y=15$. To make $20XY$ as small as possible take $X$ as small as possible, $X=6$, $Y=9$: $2069$. (Numbers $2024$ to $2059$ have $X+Y\le 5+9=14$.)

**Answer: 2069**

arml-2023-superrelay-02.title: Vieta
arml-2023-superrelay-02.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 1, which is 2069.)*

$K=2+0+6+9=17$. By Vieta, $r+s=18$ and $rs=17$, so $|r-s|=\sqrt{(r+s)^2-4rs}=\sqrt{324-68}=\sqrt{256}=16$ (indeed the roots are $1$ and $17$).

**Answer: 16**

arml-2023-superrelay-03.title: Intersection is a quarter square
arml-2023-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 2, which is 16.)*

Let each square have side $2x$. Because the center of each square is a vertex of the other (and the sides are parallel), the intersection is a square of side $x$, with area $x^2$. The union has area $(2x)^2+(2x)^2-x^2=7x^2$. The ratio is $\frac{7x^2}{x^2}=7$, independent of $T$.

**Answer: 7**

arml-2023-superrelay-04.title: Restart at each square
arml-2023-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 3, which is 7.)*

$K=63$. At a perfect square $m^2$ the sequence resets to $A_{m^2}=m$, and then increases by $1$ each step until the next square. So for $m^2\le n<(m+1)^2$, $A_n=m+(n-m^2)$. The largest square not exceeding $63$ is $49=7^2$, so $A_{63}=7+(63-49)=21$.

**Answer: 21**

arml-2023-superrelay-05.title: Divisor count
arml-2023-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 4, which is 21.)*

$20^{21}\cdot23^{21}=2^{42}\cdot5^{21}\cdot23^{21}$, which has $K=(42+1)(21+1)(21+1)=43\cdot22^2=43\cdot2^2\cdot11^2$ divisors. The greatest prime factor of $K$ is $43$.

**Answer: 43**

arml-2023-superrelay-06.title: Symmetry of binomial coefficients
arml-2023-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 5, which is 43.)*

$\binom{40}{17}=\binom{40}{40-17}=\binom{40}{23}$, so $n=23$ (the only other solution, since $\binom{40}{k}$ is strictly increasing for $k\le20$).

**Answer: 23**

arml-2023-superrelay-07.title: Cycle of units digits
arml-2023-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 6, which is 23.)*

Units digits of powers of a number cycle with period dividing $4$. Since $2023\equiv23\equiv3\pmod4$, $T^{2023}$ and $T^{23}$ have the same units digit, so $T^{2023}-T^{23}$ ends in $0$. The answer is the units digit of $23^{20}$, which is that of $3^{20}=(3^4)^5=81^5$: $1$.

**Answer: 1**

arml-2023-superrelay-08.title: Right triangle
arml-2023-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the Super Relay, the two numbers received were the answers to problem 7 (which is 1) and problem 9 (which is 5); the lesser is $r=1$ and the greater $R=5$.)*

Internal tangency gives $AB=R-r=4$. Since $BP$ is tangent to the smaller circle at $P$, $AP\perp BP$, $AP=r=1$. So $BP=\sqrt{AB^2-AP^2}=\sqrt{16-1}=\sqrt{15}$. (In general $BP=\sqrt{R^2-2Rr}$.)

**Answer: $\sqrt{15}$**

arml-2023-superrelay-09.title: Units digits
arml-2023-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 10, which is 7.)*

$T+10=17$ has the same units digit as $T=7$, and $2023\equiv23\pmod4$, so $7^{2023}$ and $17^{23}$ have the same units digit and cancel mod $10$. The answer is the units digit of $5^{20}$, which is $5$.

**Answer: 5**

arml-2023-superrelay-10.title: Slant height
arml-2023-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 11, which is 4.)*

The base has area $4$, so side $2$ (and half-side $x=1$). Let $M$ be the midpoint of $EO$; $LM\perp EO$ (the pyramid is right and $LE=LO$), and $LM=\sqrt{LE^2-EM^2}=\sqrt{50-1}=7$. Then $[LEO]=\frac12\cdot2\cdot7=7$.

**Answer: 7**

arml-2023-superrelay-11.title: Change of base
arml-2023-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 12, which is 16.)*

$\log_4T=\frac{\log_2T}{\log_24}=\frac12\log_2T=\log_2\sqrt T$, so $x=\sqrt T=4$.

**Answer: 4**

arml-2023-superrelay-13.title: Factor
arml-2023-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 14, which is $\frac78$.)*

$m=7$, $n=8$ and $x^2+15x+56=(x+7)(x+8)$, with roots $-7$ and $-8$. The lesser is $-8$.

**Answer: $-8$**

arml-2023-superrelay-14.title: Complement
arml-2023-superrelay-14.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 15, which is 3.)*

The probability of all heads is $\left(\frac12\right)^3=\frac18$, so the probability of at least one tail is $1-\frac18=\frac78$.

**Answer: $\frac78$**

arml-2023-superrelay-15.title: Two right triangles
arml-2023-superrelay-15.body:
*(In the Super Relay, the answer to this problem, 3, was passed on as $T$ for problem 14; this problem itself uses no earlier answer.)*

In right triangle $ILG$: $IG=\sqrt{IL^2-LG^2}=\sqrt{41-25}=4$. In right triangle $IGK$: $GK=\sqrt{IK^2-IG^2}=\sqrt{25-16}=3$.

**Answer: 3**
